bibliographic.title: Understanding and managing blockchain protocol risks
bibliographic.authors: Alex Nathan; Dimosthenis Kaponis; Saul Lustgarten
bibliographic.venue: Journal of Risk Management in Financial Institutions
bibliographic.citation_apa: Nathan, A., Kaponis, D., & Lustgarten, S. (2023). Understanding and managing blockchain protocol risks. Journal of Risk Management in Financial Institutions, 16(4), 337–353.

methodology.method_family: practice paper presenting collaborative risk management framework with illustrative use cases
methodology.study_design: conceptual framework development with real-world use case demonstrations
methodology.sample_description: developed in collaboration with financial institutions, blockchain development teams and regulators; no empirical participant sample described in provided text
methodology.technology_context: blockchain; distributed ledger technology (DLT); smart contracts; decentralised applications

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The article addresses blockchain protocol risk management for DLT adoption by financial institutions; the provided text contains no focus on large language models, generative AI, conversational systems, chatbots, agents, or conversational governance.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the paper offers a regulated-sector risk management framework with governance, compliance, monitoring and reporting themes, its technology context is blockchain/DLT rather than LLM-based conversational systems. Machine learning appears only in an author biography, not as the study subject. Conversational AI terms are absent from the evidence.

appraisal.notes: Practice paper proposing a structured identify-measure-monitor-report framework for blockchain protocol risks; rigor is appropriate for a practitioner framework but empirical sampling, ethics and explicit limitations are not evident in the provided excerpts.

cerqual.explanation: The framework is internally coherent for blockchain protocol risk management in financial institutions, but relevance to conversational governance in LLM systems is very low based on the supplied text.

coding.theme: Blockchain protocol risk management in regulated financial institutions
coding.subtheme: KRIs, monitoring and compliance reporting for DLT networks

synthesis.main_claim: Blockchain protocol risks require a traditional risk management taxonomy adapted for DLT so financial institutions can identify, measure, monitor and report risks affecting adoption of blockchain networks.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a collaborative practitioner framework, risk categories, KRIs, data sources and use cases for managing overlooked blockchain protocol risks beyond AML/KYC-focused concerns.
synthesis.limitations: Explicit study limitations are not described in the provided text; certification and governance equivalents for blockchain systems remain immature compared with traditional vendors.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude as central or supporting evidence for conversational LLM governance; at most distant contextual background on regulated financial risk monitoring unless the review broadens beyond conversational AI.

evidence.claim: Framework follows identify, measure, monitor and report cycle with compliance reporting
